The description contains negative or caveated signals that the criterion prohibits:
1. "For a steadier hold, attach the frame to your mask with double-sided tape or thread." This implies the product is not secure on its own and only works well with extra handling. It addresses the reviews saying the brackets "won't stay in place" and "difficult to keep in place."
2. "Extra space in front of your mouth means less pressure against your lips, so talking and breathing feel more comfortable." This addresses the reviews saying the product was "uncomfortable" and that the reviewer "could not talk and wear it." The word "more comfortable" is a minimizing reassurance that concedes the discomfort issue exists.
Under the strict standard, where any hedge, special-care condition, or minimizing reassurance about a complaint counts, the description fails.
